gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Malta produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each historical point using that point's OWN contemporaneous EUR/USD rate (monthly resolution, from FRED's DEXUSEU series, which starts 1999-01, the euro's launch). This series starts in 1995 (Maltese lira figures before 2008 converted at 0.429300 per euro), so the earliest few points predate DEXUSEU and fall back to the earliest rate DEXUSEU provides (1999-01), disclosed in the page's toggle note if it applies.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to Malta's real (chained-volume, inflation-adjusted) GDP series (Eurostat's, via FRED series CLVMNACSCAB1GQMT, from 2000). This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.source: Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CP_MEUR) · current prices, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarterly, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum.

gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, shown in chained-volume terms, the same production, valued at constant prices, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.dollar: Same historical-rate matching as GDP (current prices): each point converted at its own contemporaneous EUR/USD rate where available (1999 onward), falling back to the earliest available rate (1999-01) for anything before that.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.source: FRED series CLVMNACSCAB1GQMT (Eurostat namq_10_gdp) · chain-linked volumes, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarterly from 2000, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum.

gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real (inflation-adjusted) terms.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying euros to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.source: Derived from FRED series CLVMNACSCAB1GQMT (Eurostat namq_10_gdp) · real GDP, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarter-on-quarter, from 2000.

cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago, on the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB uses. The NSO also publishes a national retail price index, which can differ. The European Central Bank targets 2% inflation for the euro area as a whole.
cpi.source: FRED series CP0000MTM086NEST · HICP, all items, year on year.

bond_yield_10y.description: The yield on 10-year Maltese government bonds, a market gauge of inflation and interest-rate expectations. This is not the ECB's own policy rate.
bond_yield_10y.source: Eurostat irt_lt_mcby_m · long-term interest rate for convergence purposes, 10-year government bond, monthly average.

unemployment.description: The share of people aged 15 to 74 in the labour force who want a job and are actively looking, but can't find one. Jobsplus's registered unemployment is a different measure.
unemployment.source: Eurostat une_rt_m · unemployment rate, ILO definition, ages 15 to 74, seasonally adjusted, monthly.

participation_rate.description: The share of people aged 15-64 who are either working or actively looking for work.
participation_rate.source: Eurostat lfsi_emp_q · Labour Force Survey activity rate, ages 15-64, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.

employment_rate.description: The share of people aged 15-64 who are actually in work, regardless of whether others are looking.
employment_rate.source: Eurostat lfsi_emp_q · Labour Force Survey employment rate, ages 15-64, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.

trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods each month. Below zero means Malta buys more goods from abroad than it sells.
trade_balance.dollar: Each historical point is converted at its own contemporaneous EUR/USD rate (monthly resolution from FRED's DEXUSEU, 1999 onward), with the same pre-1999 earliest-rate fallback as GDP, see the GDP entry for detail.
trade_balance.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · goods trade, total, monthly, not seasonally adjusted (the plain trade value, not Eurostat's seasonally and calendar adjusted variant).

debt_gdp.description: Everything Malta's central government, local governments and social security funds owe combined, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
debt_gdp.source: Eurostat gov_10dd_edpt1 · EDP notification table, general government, % of GDP, annual.

deficit.description: The yearly gap between government spending and revenue across all levels of government, as a share of GDP. Negative means a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
deficit.source: Eurostat gov_10dd_edpt1 · EDP notification table, general government, % of GDP, annual.

ecb_rate.description: The European Central Bank's key interest rate, the anchor for borrowing costs across the euro area, including Malta, which joined the euro on 1 January 2008 and has had no policy rate of its own since. Shown from 2008. This is the deposit facility rate specifically, one of the ECB's three main policy rates.

cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the month, on the EU's harmonised measure. A monthly change is not the annual rate divided by twelve: it is the change on the month before, so it moves with one-off price changes that the annual rate smooths out.
cpi_mom.source: Derived from FRED series CP0000MTM086NEST (Eurostat) · HICP, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted.

fx_usd.description: How many US dollars €1 buys. A rising number means a stronger euro. The euro is shared across the euro area, so this is the same series as the Eurozone's.
fx_usd.source: FRED series DEXUSEU (Federal Reserve H.10) · end-of-month rate, the current month shows the latest daily rate; shown as US$ per €1, as published.

fx_gbp.description: How many pounds €1 buys. A rising number means a stronger euro.
fx_gbp.source: Derived from Federal Reserve H.10 series DEXUSEU and DEXUSUK (FRED) on each trading day, end of month; £ per €1 = (US$ per €1) ÷ (US$ per £1).
